set.body:
Collapse `multivar` to a single typed operator layer. Source of truth: docs/plans/multivar-operator-core.md — the committed target that supersedes the dual-layer arrangement in docs/plans/multivar-duality-constitution.md (the constitution's 12 invariants stay binding).

Problem: `multivar` carries two parallel representations of the same math — a semantic operator layer (Lin/Table/Coordinate/GeometricOperator/SemanticDualityDiagram) and a legacy numeric mirror (MvMetric/DualityDiagram/MvMap + the raw GenPca engine) that is what actually computes. SemanticGenPca.fit prepares the typed diagram then drops to legacyDiagram + GenPca.fit. On top of that seam sits a zoo of per-method estimators (six named GenPCA result records; PairedGmd as a private third engine). The basis is right; the layering is not. Because the library is new with no external consumers, we take the one move a behavior-preserving refactor cannot: collapse to one layer and DELETE the legacy compute path.

Target (see doc): one `Op[From,To,Role]` with the numeric kernel inside it; two primitives — `secondOrder` (Xˢ·L·X pullback) and `compress` (Wˢ·S·W) — as the only ways second-order/component operators arise; one `FunctionalFrame` (scores=XW, axes=QW derived); the base objective a closed enum; methods as named constructors. Bells and whistles (sparsity/smoothness/shrinkage/low-rank/nonneg/agreement) are never new methods — they are structural TERMS (a functional or a feasible set pulled back through a typed target) plus upstream operator POLICIES, kept as five distinct first-class concepts, never one "transformation".

Invariants, green on BOTH JVM and Scala.js after every phase: GenPCA + PairedLatent R parity fixtures pass unchanged (the numbers are the invariant); the multivar-ir conformance corpus passes; `sbt testAll` clean; shared multivar imports no Breeze/dataset/image/scheduler/binding runtime.

Structure (child issues):
- Phase 1 — core collapse: P1a primitives (Op + secondOrder/compress + FunctionalFrame); P1b re-base GenPCA and delete the legacy path; P1c extend the wire IR.
- Phase 2 — LDA via secondOrder (proof the pullback generalizes on new code).
- Phase 3 — paired family (PLSC/CCA/RRR) through the primitives; delete PairedGmd.
- Phase 4 — multiset/direct-sum through secondOrder; promote MultisetObjectives to the universal objective+term layer.
- Phase 5 — the variational term layer (penalties/constraints/policies/parameterizations), built family-by-family, each with a solver lowering + a parity fixture.

When Phase 4 lands, the dual-layer language leaves the constitution and the doc becomes its implemented "operator core" section; Phase 5 accretes under it without reopening the core.
set.title: Epic: multivar operator-core — one typed operator layer, legacy numeric mirror deleted
